findings.finding: drivers: [firecracker] understates the plan's reach. The plan changes the relay binary: relay-to-host vsock signals for 'CA ready' and 'ledger complete' (firecracker-driver-plan.md:381, 'This minimizes changes to the relay binary'). It also shares helpers with qemu (util.go, line 801). FLOW-02 says a change to a shared package declares every dependent driver. The design's own Decision 5 (design-front-matter-retrofit.md:86) applies that rule to hyperv-driver-plan (relay/) and windows-driver-plan (cmd/warden-io), but not here.
findings.suggestion: drivers: [container, qemu, vz, hyperv, firecracker]  # relay/ gains vsock signaling. Amend the block at design-front-matter-retrofit.md:181 first, then the file.

findings.finding: seams omits relay-claim. The plan injects per-build relay config (relay.env, line 442), extracts the CA cert from the relay (line 449), and the warm pool injects build-specific config into a resumed relay over vsock (line 660). GLOBAL-08 defines the claim protocol as exactly this: per-build config pushed to the relay, relay identity and ca.cert.pem returned. A plan for an alternative config path is a claim-seam change, and the most likely retrieval key for the firecracker-driver design.
findings.suggestion: seams: [relay-claim, relay-guest-api, collector]  # config/CA via rootfs or vsock predate relaycfg; outputs from relay rootfs predate RELAY-07

findings.finding: security_boundary: env-relay, but the document has no security note. The YAML comment says so ('no separate security section'). FLOW-02: 'Any value other than none requires a security note in the design.' Decision 6 points the comment at an existing security section where one exists. Here none does, so the retrofit leaves a front-matter that violates the rule it implements. a4 ('front-matter only') does not tell Jeff that this is a consequence for this document.
findings.suggestion: Design decision, not an implement fix. Either (a) a4 option (b)-style: a short security note (2-3 lines) after the front-matter naming the boundary touched (guest CA trust-store install via certutil; topological isolation in the relay VM, no guest firewall), or (b) state the exception explicitly in the design and in a4 so Jeff's confirmation covers it, then suppress this finding with that reason.

findings.finding: Same as windows-driver-plan.md:9. security_boundary: env-relay with 'no security section yet' and no security note. This document is draft, so the first design that builds on it inherits a non-none boundary with no note. The proposal changes the relay itself: the relay ledger incorporates records from cached sub-ledgers it did not observe. GLOBAL-06 makes any change to the relay high-severity regardless.
findings.suggestion: As for windows-driver-plan.md:9: a one-paragraph security note (relay incorporates unobserved sub-ledger records; the cache and CAS become trusted provenance inputs; the RE API is a new network-facing service), or an explicit exception recorded in the design and confirmed under a4.

findings.finding: status: archived hides unbuilt scope. The plan's own Phase 1 is 'Skeleton + Linux guest' (line 1491) and it has a Linux Guest Provisioning section (line 685). vm-driver-release-plan.md:495 says 'Linux guests on Hyper-V not started'. The design's problem table calls it 'implemented'. A future design searching drivers: [hyperv] would read the Linux-guest path as done. FLOW-12's letter is met (merged plans are archived), so this is advisory.
findings.suggestion: Keep archived and add a comment, e.g. status: archived  # Windows guests built; Linux guests on Hyper-V not built (vm-driver-release-plan Phase 5). Or use active if Jeff treats it as the live plan for Linux guests.

findings.finding: native_validation does not match the conservative drivers list. drivers declares container, qemu, vz and hyperv because cmd/warden-io is shared, and the plan itself requires a regression check on the VZ and Linux+qemu paths (lines 105-109). native_validation names only macos-qemu (for win-arm64) and windows-hyperv. hyperv-driver-plan.md:11 has the same gap for its relay/ change. Decision 7 makes these descriptive, but a reader would conclude vz needed no native run.
findings.suggestion: Add {host: macos-vz, blocking: false, reason: "plan's cross-contamination check: VZ path untouched by Windows changes"} and widen the macos-qemu reason to cover Linux+qemu; or add a comment that only the plan's primary hosts are listed.

informational.note: alters_relationships: true is the conservative choice (a3 a). Under a3 (b) it could fairly be false: it moves Windows guest code from two drivers into shared driver/winguest, inside the orchestrator/driver role, and its seams are not GLOBAL-08 versioned seams. No tool reads design front-matter status or alters_relationships (only queue/*.yaml feeds the FLOW-05 limit), so neither value has an operational effect. ledger-environment-types (ledger-format, relay-claim) and unified-bootstrap (bootstrap-model) are clearly true.
